practices.practice: Read the DocumentDB MongoDB connection string from an environment variable at runtime and avoid committing credentials or secrets to source control or logs.
practices.prior_belief: Read the DocumentDB connection string from an environment variable (DOCUMENTDB_URI) at runtime and never commit the URI or any credentials to source control or logs; provide only a .env.example placeholder.

practices.practice: Create one long-lived MongoClient per process (singleton) and reuse it rather than creating a new client per request.
practices.prior_belief: Use a single long-lived MongoClient instance per process (create one MongoClient and reuse it for all requests) rather than creating a new client per request or operation.

practices.practice: Always require TLS for client connections and do not disable certificate verification in production.
practices.prior_belief: Ensure TLS/SSL is enabled for connections (require server certificate verification) and reject insecure connections; enforce tls=true/tlsAllowInvalidCertificates=false in connection options.

practices.practice: Tune connection-pool and timeout settings to match your deployment pattern (serverless vs long-running server) and initialize the client outside request handlers for serverless warm-invocations.
practices.prior_belief: Configure reasonable connection pool and timeouts on the MongoClient (e.g., maxPoolSize tuned to app concurrency, set connectTimeoutMS and socketTimeoutMS) instead of relying on defaults.

practices.practice: Implement retries with exponential backoff for transient errors and specifically detect and respect throttling responses (HTTP 429 / service-specific codes) and any Retry-After guidance.
practices.prior_belief: Implement exponential backoff retries for transient network errors and throttling responses; specifically detect 429 (throttling) responses and respect any Retry-After header before retrying.

practices.practice: Use upsert/replace operations for idempotent writes (prefer updateOne/replaceOne/replace with upsert) so repeated retries do not create duplicates.
practices.prior_belief: Make writes idempotent by using unique request identifiers and upserts (findOneAndUpdate with upsert or updateOne with upsert and $set) so repeated retries won’t create duplicates.
practices.source_name: Quickstart and reliability docs on Azure DocumentDB (upsert examples and retry guidance)

practices.practice: Create indexes on fields used in query predicates and sorts and prefer carefully-shaped compound (ESR) indexes for filter+sort patterns to avoid collection scans.
practices.prior_belief: Create indexes on all fields used in predicates and sorts for hot queries (e.g., requestId, patientId, status, createdAt) and create compound indexes for filters+sort combinations to avoid COLLSCAN.

practices.practice: Create a dedicated vector index (choose DiskANN / HNSW / IVF by scale), set the index kind, similarity and dimensions to match your embeddings, and tune build/query parameters for recall/latency tradeoffs.
practices.prior_belief: For vector-enabled queries, create and configure a dedicated vector index on the embedding field (explicitly specify index type and metric) and keep embedding dimensionality consistent across documents.

practices.practice: Store embeddings in a dedicated field with the embedding model name and dimensions; normalize embeddings when using cosine similarity and rebuild indexes if you change the encoder or dimensions.
practices.prior_belief: Precompute and store text embeddings (and normalize them if necessary) rather than computing on every query; store embeddings in a dedicated field and version the embedding schema if you change the encoder.

practices.practice: If documents contain very large fields (long text or blobs) split the large field into a side collection keyed by _id so the hot collection stays small and avoids PostgreSQL detoast costs.
Use TTL indexes for ephemeral documents (drafts, caches) to automatically expire old data rather than relying on manual cleanup jobs.
practices.prior_belief: Use TTL indexes for ephemeral data (drafts, temporary caches) to automatically expire old documents instead of manual cleanup tasks.

practices.practice: Use explain('executionStats') and slow-query diagnostics (enable diagnostic settings → Log Analytics) to verify index usage, detect COLLSCANs, and feed top slow queries back into index design.
practices.prior_belief: Monitor queries and indexes using explain() and the server profiler; add indexes for high-frequency queries revealed by explain and remove unused indexes that waste RU/storage.

practices.practice: Prefer least-privilege credentials: use Microsoft Entra ID / RBAC or per-app users with only the roles required rather than using cluster admin credentials in applications.
practices.prior_belief: Use least-privilege database credentials: create a dedicated DB user with only the required roles (readWrite on sample_healthcare_08) instead of using an admin/root account in the app.

practices.practice: Make seeding and local init scripts safe and idempotent (use upserts, gate destructive ops behind explicit flags, and drive config from env vars) so they can be run repeatedly in dev without data loss.
practices.prior_belief: Make seeding scripts idempotent: create collections and createIndex calls should be safe to run multiple times and should not drop production data; gate destructive operations behind explicit flags.

practices.practice: Separate fast unit tests (mocking MongoClient) from integration tests that run against a live DocumentDB cluster and gate live tests with env variables or CI flags.
practices.prior_belief: When running tests, separate fast unit tests (mocking MongoClient) from integration tests that exercise the live DocumentDB cluster and gate live tests with environment variables or CI flags.

practices.practice: Choose readPreference / read routing to match consistency needs (use primary for strongly consistent reads and prefer nearest or secondaryPreferred for analytics/non-critical reads).
practices.prior_belief: Set an appropriate readPreference (primary for strongly consistent reads used by the orchestrator when reading newly written submissions; secondaryPreferred for analytics or non-critical reads) to match consistency needs.

practices.practice: Prefer DocumentDB-native full-text search (createSearchIndexes + $search) rather than community text indexes and $text if you need BM25, custom analyzers, fuzzy/phrase search or hybrid BM25+vector retrieval.

Monitor request-unit / throughput and latency metrics (RequestCharge, NormalizedRUConsumption) and alert on saturation or 429s; measure RU per-query (RequestCharge) especially for vector queries and scope queries to partitions to avoid cross-partition fan-out.
practices.source_name: Azure DocumentDB / Cosmos DB monitoring and vector-search guidance
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB vector search RU monitoring

practices.practice: Use the MongoDB-compatible server's JSON Schema validation ($jsonSchema) at collection-level to enforce required fields and types where appropriate.
Keep transactions short and use multi-document transactions only when you must update multiple documents atomically; prefer single-document atomic updates for simple status changes.
practices.prior_belief: When updating status and storing the final submission, prefer single-document atomic updates (updateOne with $set) or use a transaction only if you must update multiple collections atomically; keep transactions short.

practices.practice: Use explain and query metrics to shape queries so they return only needed fields and avoid scanning large fields; project/limit fields to reduce network bandwidth and RU costs where possible.
practices.prior_belief: Project only necessary fields in queries (use projection) when reading documents (e.g., exclude large fields like full clinical notes or embeddings when not needed) to reduce bandwidth and RU costs.

practices.practice: Do not store very large binary/PDF blobs inline in a hot collection; for Azure DocumentDB public guidance, prefer splitting very large fields into a side collection keyed by _id rather than co-locating large blobs in frequently-scanned collections.
practices.prior_belief: Limit document size: do not embed large binary or PDF blobs in documents; instead store large files in blob storage (Azure Blob) and include a reference (URL or id) in the DocumentDB document.

practices.practice: If you need JSON Schema enforcement, use the service's $jsonSchema / schema-validation features to declare required fields and types at collection creation or with validation rules.
practices.prior_belief: Use collection-level JSON Schema validation to enforce required fields and types for pre-auth requests and submission documents (e.g., require requestId, patientId, status, createdAt, embedding shape).

practices.practice: Instrument throughput/metrics (RequestCharge / NormalizedRUConsumption) and alert on CPU/memory/IOPS/storage/connection saturation; track RU per-query to detect hot partitions and expensive vector queries.
practices.prior_belief: Instrument RU/throughput and latency metrics for the collection (or database) and adjust provisioned throughput or query patterns to avoid throttling—watch vector queries for high RU consumption.
practices.source_name: Azure DocumentDB monitoring / vector-search RU guidance
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB / vector search RU monitoring

practices.practice: Pin and use a MongoDB driver version that supports the server's wire protocol and features you rely on (verify supported wire protocol versions for your cluster tier before enabling features like vector search).
practices.prior_belief: Ensure your MongoDB driver version is compatible with the server wire protocol (use a driver supporting MongoDB 7.0 features if you rely on 7.0 vector/search features) and pin the dependency in package.json.

practices.practice: Use optimistic concurrency control (version/ETag or conditional updates) to prevent lost updates when multiple clients may concurrently modify the same document; implement conditional updates or version filters as needed.
practices.source_name: Azure Cosmos DB / DocumentDB concurrency guidance (ETag/If-Match patterns)
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB optimistic concurrency guidance (ETag / If-Match)

practices.practice: Do not log PHI or sensitive patient data and redact or exclude identifying fields from diagnostics and logs; ensure log retention and access meet compliance requirements.
practices.prior_belief: Avoid storing PHI in logs and redact sensitive fields before any diagnostic logging or error reports; ensure the app’s log retention and access controls meet privacy/regulatory requirements.
practices.how_found: searches run: "Azure DocumentDB PHI logging best practices"; "DocumentDB redact logs PHI"; "Azure DocumentDB compliance logging guidance"

practices.practice: Persist intermediate orchestrator state (reviewResult, letterDraft) so orchestrator logic is resumable and idempotent, allowing retries without duplication.
practices.prior_belief: Write idempotent, resumable orchestrator logic: persist intermediate state (e.g., reviewResult, letterDraft) with timestamps so the orchestrator can resume or retry without duplication if interrupted.
practices.how_found: searches run: "Azure DocumentDB orchestrator persisted state resume retries"; "idempotent orchestrator pattern DocumentDB"

practices.practice: When updating shuffled/competing documents concurrently use optimistic concurrency (version) or a conditional findOneAndUpdate with version-check to avoid lost updates; the service itself does not mandate a single pattern so implement per-app.
practices.prior_belief: For concurrent updates to the same submission, use optimistic concurrency control (e.g., a version number or updatedAt + conditional update) or findOneAndUpdate with a filter on the current version to prevent lost updates.
practices.how_found: searches run: "Azure DocumentDB optimistic concurrency ETag If-Match DocumentDB"; "DocumentDB conditional update version field"
